Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Chromatin persistence after AP-1 washout
ideas.description: Pulse cells with a stimulus, then wash it out and track AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN for c-Jun/c-Fos) alongside ATAC-seq and H3K27ac over days. If accessibility and enhancer marks outlast AP-1 binding, the 'fire' is being carried by chromatin rather than by the transcription factor itself, which is the core prediction of a memory mechanism.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 depletion during the inter-stimulus interval
ideas.description: Prime cells with one stimulus, then use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron on Fos or Jun to remove AP-1 during the rest period before a second stimulus. Memory is defined as a faster or stronger re-induction; if the primed advantage disappears only when AP-1 is degraded during the gap, AP-1 is required to store the memory rather than just to read it out.

ideas.title: Mutating AP-1 motifs at primed enhancers
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing to mutate AP-1 motifs on individual primed enhancers, mirroring each mutation on a matched control enhancer to keep the design symmetric. Then measure whether the enhancer's persistence of accessibility, H3K27ac and re-induction kinetics are lost, which tests whether motif occupancy at specific loci is necessary for the memory.

ideas.title: Lineage-resolved tracking of primed states through division
ideas.description: Combine an AP-1-responsive fluorescent reporter with lineage barcoding and time-lapse imaging to follow single cells after priming. Ask whether the primed state is inherited by daughter cells and whether it fades in the absence of reactivation, which distinguishes a self-sustaining epigenetic memory from a transient signaling state that is simply reset.

ideas.title: Protein turnover and bistability modeling
ideas.description: Measure the half-lives of Fos, Jun and Fra1 with SNAP/HaloTag pulse-chase and FRAP, then build a kinetic model with and without an AP-1-dependent feedback loop. Test whether the model with a feedback loop predicts a long-lived, bistable primed state that persists for longer than protein turnover alone allows, and whether that prediction holds in the unstimulated dark state.
